name: Gastrodia rhizome (Gastrodia elata)
short: Trial of Gastrodia elata extract, 80 adults with memory complaints: no serious adverse events. Gastrodin, its main component (partly injected): 1 trial, no drug-related events; 1 review unsure.
text: In a 12-week randomised, placebo-controlled trial of Gastrodia elata extract in 80 adults with subjective memory complaints, no serious adverse events occurred; the abstract does not describe milder adverse events. Most other human data concern gastrodin, the main component of Gastrodia elata, rather than the whole rhizome: a meta-analysis of 16 randomised trials (1,332 participants) in migraine described gastrodin as safe, but its abstract gives no adverse-event figures and does not state the route or comparator, while a meta-analysis of 8 trials in tension-type headache, covering capsules and injections, found that only one trial detailed adverse reactions and so could not reach a conclusion on safety. In a randomised placebo-controlled trial of gastrodin given by infusion around heart bypass surgery (155 patients analysed), adverse events occurred in 9.1% with gastrodin and 14.1% with placebo, none of them drug-related. A 2016 review of the rhizome called for more toxicological study in humans to validate its safety in clinical use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
